subtitle: The social glue — aisatsu, register ladders, untranslatables
notes: The set phrases textbooks romanize on page one and never drill: home/leaving pairs, meal pairs, the すみません triple-duty, the お疲れ様 workplace economy, and politeness escalation ladders.
source: Hand-authored for Kanjido v1 (factual common-knowledge Japanese expressions).

cards.context: Drop ございます with friends/family: おはよう. In workplaces it greets the FIRST meeting of the day even at night — service industry uses it at 8 PM.
Written with は (the particle), pronounced わ. Daytime only, and NOT used with your own in-group (family, close coworkers) — it has built-in distance.
Same は-spelling trap as こんにちは.
Casual: おやすみ. Said when someone is going to bed OR when parting at night.
Heavier than textbooks suggest — can imply long/permanent separation. Everyday partings: じゃあね, またね, お先に失礼します (work).
The actual everyday goodbye between friends. Variants: じゃ、また / またね / バイバイ.
Pairs with おかえりなさい. Literally 'just now (returned)'.
Response to ただいま. Casual: おかえり.
Said when leaving home/office. Literally 'I'll go and come back' — the coming-back is built into the grammar.
Response to いってきます.
Humble 'I receive'. Thanks everyone and everything that produced the meal. No English equivalent — 'bon appétit' is said TO others; this is said by the eater.
Closes the いただきます pair. Said to hosts, restaurant staff on leaving, or whoever paid. Casual: ごちそうさま.

cards.word: ありがとうございます
cards.reading: ありがとうございます
cards.context: Past tense ありがとうございました thanks a COMPLETED favor. Present tense for ongoing/just-now ones. Casual: ありがとう.
Triple duty: getting attention, light apology, AND thanks-with-apology (someone holds the door → すみません). The single most useful word in spoken Japanese.
cards.example_sentence: すみません、駅はどこですか。
cards.example_reading: すみません、えき は どこ です か。
cards.example_meaning: Excuse me, where is the station?

cards.context: More personal than すみません, used with people close to you. Casual: ごめん／ごめんね. For serious/business apologies: 申し訳ありません.

cards.reading: もうしわけありません
cards.context: Business-grade apology — literally 'there is no excuse'. The escalation ladder: ごめん → すみません → 申し訳ありません → 申し訳ございません.
Attach to anything you're requesting: これ、お願いします (this one, please). よろしくお願いします is its own separate beast — see that card.

cards.word: よろしくお願いします
cards.reading: よろしくおねがいします
cards.context: Untranslatable glue phrase: ends self-introductions, requests, emails, year-end greetings. Means roughly 'please treat the relationship/task well'. Just learn the situations, not a translation.
Only at FIRST meetings. Standard set: はじめまして。[name]です。よろしくお願いします。
The workplace everything-greeting: passing coworkers, starting calls, ending meetings, leaving (お疲れ様でした). Never to customers — that's ありがとうございました.
cards.example_sentence: お先に失礼します。— お疲れ様でした。
cards.example_reading: おさき に しつれい します。— おつかれさまでした。
cards.example_meaning: I'm heading out first. — Good work today.

cards.reading: おさきにしつれいします
cards.context: Said when leaving the office while others are still working. The reply is お疲れ様でした.
Entering an office or someone's room, hanging up a phone, leaving a meeting. Literally 'I commit a rudeness'. Past tense 失礼しました doubles as a light apology.
You HEAR this constantly but never say it (staff only). No response needed — a nod is fine. Don't reply こんにちは.
Staff-speak for 'understood'. The politeness ladder: 分かった → 分かりました → 承知しました → かしこまりました.

cards.reading: しょうしょうおまちください
cards.context: Shop and phone staple. Casual version: ちょっと待って(ね).
Said when returning to a customer/friend after any wait — even a short one. Restaurant servers say it delivering food.
The offering word: handing things over, yielding a seat, inviting someone in. Pairs with どうも as the reply.
Swiss-army filler: light thanks, casual hello, soft acknowledgment. どうもどうも from a middle-aged man can be an entire conversation.
Casual: 久しぶり！ Roughly after a month or more apart.
NOT a daily greeting like English 'how are you' — only for people you haven't seen in a while. Reply: はい、元気です or おかげさまで.
The graceful answer to お元気ですか — credits your wellbeing to others' kindness. Standalone: おかげさまで、元気です。
To anyone ill or leaving a hospital/pharmacy. Full: お大事になさってください.
Seeing someone off: (お)気をつけて(ください). Also literal 'watch out!'.
Encouragement before exams/games/work. Casual: 頑張って／頑張れ. Reply: 頑張ります. To someone already struggling hard, 無理しないで (don't overdo it) is kinder.
cards.example_sentence: 明日の試験、頑張ってください。
cards.example_reading: あした の しけん、がんばって ください。

cards.word: おめでとうございます
cards.reading: おめでとうございます
cards.context: 誕生日おめでとう (birthday), 合格おめでとう (passing an exam), 明けましておめでとう (New Year).

cards.word: 明けましておめでとうございます
cards.reading: あけましておめでとうございます
cards.context: Only AFTER midnight on Jan 1. Before year-end you say よいお年を. Followed by 今年もよろしくお願いします.

meanings: have a good New Year (said in December)
cards.context: The BEFORE-new-year farewell — don't mix up with 明けまして (after).
Phone-only. Business calls open with お電話ありがとうございます or 「会社名」でございます instead.
Said stepping into someone's home — literally 'I will disturb you'. Leaving: お邪魔しました.
Welcoming guests/visitors: 日本へようこそ = Welcome to Japan.
Deflects praise or thanks. Politer than いいえいいえ; the natural reply when a compliment lands.
Returns a thanks or greeting: ありがとう → こちらこそ (no, thank YOU).
Modern double duty: 'I'm fine' AND a soft 'no thanks' (レジ袋は？→ 大丈夫です). Context and tone decide — a major listening-comprehension trap.
cards.example_sentence: 袋はご利用ですか。— 大丈夫です。
cards.example_reading: ふくろ は ごりよう です か。— だいじょうぶ です。
cards.example_meaning: Do you need a bag? — No, I'm fine.

cards.word: お世話になっております
cards.reading: おせわになっております
meanings: thank you for your continued support (business)
cards.context: Opens nearly every business email and call between companies. There is no English equivalent; treat it as 'Dear sir/madam' that also does gratitude.
Textbook 'no', but real speech softens: いや、ちょっと…, うーん, or just trailing off. Blunt いいえ can sound stiff. As a reply to thanks it means 'don't mention it'.
Also the aizuchi 'uh-huh' — はい during your speech means 'I'm following', NOT 'I agree'. Contract negotiations have gone wrong over this.
